mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in INDPRO below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GDPC1 and a fall in HOUST over one quarter signals a demand shift toward services and away from housing, which favors technology and consumer discretionary sectors and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 0% QoQ and HOUST < 0% QoQ in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 rises and HOUST falls in the same quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in CPIAUCSL below 2% for two consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains below 3% signals a deflationary bias with accommodative policy, which boosts real discount rates and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0% for 2 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS < 3.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months and FEDFUNDS < 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS and a fall in UNRATE over three months indicates strong job creation with stable wage growth, supporting corporate profit margins and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0% QoQ and UNRATE < 0% QoQ over three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals robust household savings, which typically coincides with precautionary behavior and reduced consumption, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months.
